title: Product PRD: Unified Inference — Overview, Roadmap, Pricing & Release Notes (Nov 2026)
author: Ava Chen
body:
Overview:

This document consolidates the product overview, prioritized requirements (PRD), high-level design notes, roadmap themes, pricing and packaging guidance, and release notes for the Unified Inference product as of Nov 2026. It is intended for PMs, Eng leads, Sales, and GTM stakeholders.

Goals & success metrics:
- Primary goal: Provide a single developer-facing product that delivers predictable latency, cost-efficiency, and deployment flexibility across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private modes.
- Success metrics (next 6 months):
  - 30% reduction in median per-token cost for served workloads vs baseline (Q3 2026).
  - Increase self-serve adoption: 20% higher conversion of free-credit users to paid API customers.
  - Reliability: Hosted API availability >= 99.9% (monthly), Dedicated SLAs >= 99.95%.
  - Developer satisfaction (NPS of API and docs) >= 50 (internal target).

Target customers & use cases:
- AI-native startups: rapid prototyping -> scale with predictable economics.
- Mid-market/enterprise product teams: need SLAs, data controls, private deployability.
- Platform teams: standardized inference with policy-driven routing.
- Primary use cases: chat assistants, summarization for high-throughput pipelines, retrieval+generate workflows, low-latency token streaming for interactive UX.

Problem statements & user needs:
1) Cost unpredictability for high-throughput workloads: customers need clear levers (batching, caching, quantization) presented as operational controls.
2) Rollouts across environments are fragmented: teams want identical API semantics and rollout behavior from Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private.
3) Quality regressions on model rollouts: customers require eval-linked regressions and quick rollback.
4) Pricing complexity: customers need transparent packaging that maps to unit economics (tokens, embeddings, reserved capacity).

High-level product scope (what's in this release):
- Unified API primitives: text generation, chat, embeddings, reranking, function/tool calling (backwards compatible with existing SDKs).
- Cost & performance controls in console: per-route batching profiles, KV cache toggles, quantization recommendations.
- Model routing policies: latency-first, cost-first, region affinity, fallback rules for capacity constraints.
- Pricing refresh: introduce Dedicated reserved tier with commit discounts and burst credit system.
- Release automation: canary rollouts with automated rollback on quality regressions.

Requirements (functional):
1) API and SDK compatibility
  - 1.1 Backwards compatibility: existing client requests must succeed without code changes for common endpoints (generate, chat, embed).
  - 1.2 New params: support "routing_policy" and "cost_profile" as optional request fields.
2) Console controls and observability
  - 2.1 Per-route latency/cost charts and token-level breakdowns for last 90 days.
  - 2.2 Configuration UI for batching window, KV cache TTL, and quantization profile per model.
3) Model routing & fallbacks
  - 3.1 Policy engine to route by latency target, cost budget, or region.
  - 3.2 Automatic fallback to quantized model variants when capacity exceeds threshold.
4) Dedicated & Reserved pricing
  - 4.1 Offer monthly reserved GPU capacity with configurable burst credits.
  - 4.2 Billing: combine commitment fee + usage overage at discounted rate.
5) Release & quality guardrails
  - 5.1 Canary pipeline with metric checks: error rate, latency, token generation quality delta (eval suite).
  - 5.2 Rollback criteria: >1% absolute increase in error rate or >20% P95 latency regression, or >3% decrease in eval pass-rate on golden prompt-set.

Requirements (non-functional):
- NFR-1: Hosted inference median P50 latency for standard 512-token workloads <= 100ms.
- NFR-2: P95 latency <= 350ms for same workload under normal load.
- NFR-3: API availability >= 99.9% (hosted).
- NFR-4: Throughput targets for Dedicated: baseline 10k tokens/s per reserved GPU cluster unit.
- NFR-5: Observability retention: metrics 90 days, request traces 30 days (configurable add-on).

Design overview & key decisions:
- Runtime abstraction: keep same API surface while allowing routing and kernel selection to be orthogonal. Service will annotate responses with model_variant and route_reason for observability.
- Kernel & quantization profiles: maintain a profile registry (profile-id string) that maps model to supported quantization and estimated memory/cost delta; profile selection is recommended by Optimize engine and surfaceable in console.
- Routing engine: policy DSL (expressed as simple JSON in config) that supports priority lists and thresholds. Policies evaluated at request arrival; fallback is synchronous and returns telemetry.
- Canary rollouts: staged traffic shifts (5%, 20%, 50%, 100%) with automated gating checks at each stage. Canary checks include: 1) 15-minute rolling error rate, 2) rolling latency quantiles, 3) eval harness on sampled responses.

Roadmap & themes (quarterly):
- Q4 2026 (current release): Unified API + pricing refresh + console cost controls + routing policies + canary automation.
- Q1 2027: Model-level quality monitoring (automated evals), SDK improvements for simplified routing_policy usage, Dedicated provisioning automation.
- Q2 2027: Private deployment orchestration improvements (air-gapped installers), advanced batching heuristics (adaptive batching), and additional quantization profiles for new open models.
- Q3 2027: Enterprise feature set: advanced RBAC for model access, fine-grained audit trails, extended retention and compliance packages.

Pricing & packaging notes (summary):
- Hosted (pay-as-you-go): per-token pricing tiers remain; introduce "cost_profile" multiplier for models that use expensive GPU kernels (0.8x – 2.0x).
- Dedicated (reserved): monthly commit pricing with 12/36 month options. Commit includes baseline throughput; burst credits sold as add-on. Example packaging:
  - Small reserved: 4 GPU-equivalent units, $12k/mo commit, 10% discount on overage.
  - Medium reserved: 16 units, $40k/mo commit, 15% discount on overage.
  - Large reserved: 64 units, custom pricing & SLA.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): licensing + support fee. Price depends on nodes, HA topology, and support tier.
- Add-ons & enterprise extras: extended observability retention, compliance evidence bundles, dedicated support (24/7 pager).
- Billing & metering clarifications: tokens are metered at request-time, reserved commitments deduct first; overages billed monthly. Bursts are consumed from burst credits before overage billing.

Pricing rationale + examples:
- Use-case: high-throughput embedding pipeline (10M tokens/day) -> Dedicated small reserved reduces unit cost by ~30% vs Hosted YOY for steady workloads.
- Use-case: low-volume interactive chat -> Hosted pay-as-you-go favored due to bursty traffic and no commit.

Release notes — Unified Inference v3.1 (Nov 2026):
Summary: Major release delivering unified API surface, console cost controls, routing policies and pricing updates.
Highlights:
- Unified API: New optional request params routing_policy and cost_profile; SDKs v3.1 published.
- Console: Per-route batching controls and KV cache TTL wizards; token-level cost breakdown chart (last 90 days).
- Routing: Policy engine with region affinity and latency-first mode.
- Pricing: Dedicated reserved tiers and burst credits launched; updated billing flows.
- Safety & reliability: Canary automation integrated into release pipeline; default rollback thresholds applied.

Behavior changes & migration notes:
- Backwards compatibility: All existing endpoints remain supported. However new pricing semantics (cost_profile multiplier) may affect invoice totals for customers that explicitly set model_variant in requests; customers will be notified through in-console notice and email.
- Migration steps for Integrators:
  1) Upgrade SDK to v3.1 (supports routing_policy and cost_profile) — example: pip install redwood-sdk==3.1.0.
  2) Validate critical routes in staging using new canary harness.
  3) If using Dedicated reserved capacity, consult billing docs to confirm commit mapping.

Rollout plan & ownership:
- Release manager: Diego Alvarez (product-ops) — coordinates cross-functional rollout.
- PM owner: Ava Chen.
- Eng owners: Lead, Runtime: Priya Kapoor; Lead, Platform: Marco Singh; Observability lead: Chen Li.
- Release stages:
  - Internal Canary: 2026-11-06 — test within staging and limited internal workloads.
  - External Canary (5% traffic): 2026-11-09 — small set of customers opt-in.
  - Broad rollout (incremental to 100%): 2026-11-16 -> 2026-11-20 subject to canary gates.

Canary gating & rollback criteria (operational playbook):
- Monitoring windows: 15-minute rolling, 1-hour rolling, daily summary.
- Automatic fail conditions (any triggers cause automated rollback to previous model variant/service):
  - Absolute increase in error rate > 1% vs baseline.
  - P95 latency increase > 20% vs baseline.
  - Eval harness sampled pass-rate drop > 3% on golden prompt-set.
- Manual review conditions: increased latency < 20% but sustained for > 6 hours, or customer-reported quality issues.

Telemetry & dashboards to be released:
- Per-route: tokens served, cost per 1k tokens, P50/P95/P99 latency, error rate, model_variant distribution.
- Canary dashboard: rolling stats for canary cohorts plus sampled response diffs (text MRR / BLEU-like heuristics).

Open risks & mitigation:
- Risk: Customers misinterpret cost_profile multipliers -> Mitigation: in-console estimator, pre-release pricing email, and trial credits for re-evaluation.
- Risk: Quantized variants may cause subtle quality regressions -> Mitigation: require model-specific eval suites and block auto-fallback for restricted customers unless opted-in.

Action items (next 30 days):
1) Eng: finalize policy DSL schema and publish docs (owner: Marco Singh) — due 2026-11-10.
2) PM: publish customer migration playbook and pricing FAQ (owner: Ava Chen) — due 2026-11-08.
3) Sales: update pricing sheets and playbook for Dedicated (owner: Emily Brooks) — due 2026-11-12.
4) CX: prepare targeted customer notices for customers with high usage of pinned model_variants (owner: Noah Kim) — due 2026-11-09.

Appendix: Example policy JSON (console-editable) — for reference:
{
  "policy_name": "latency-first-us-west",
  "rules": [
    {"priority": 1, "match": {"region":"us-west"}, "action": {"route":"gpt-x-low-latency", "max_latency_ms":150}},
    {"priority": 2, "action": {"route":"gpt-x-cost-optimized", "max_cost_multiplier":1.0}}
  ]
}

Frequently asked questions (FAQ):
- Q: Will existing API keys change billing?
  - A: No. Billing changes apply to new billing model semantics (cost_profile & reserved commitments) and will be applied to accounts after notification.
- Q: Can customers opt out of auto-fallback to quantized models?
  - A: Yes. Dedicated and Private customers can opt-out via account settings; Hosted customers may opt-out per-route.
